name: Temporal and Procedural Techniques

text:
# Temporal and Procedural Techniques

Also called: Procedural Volume Rendering, Dynamic Volume Rendering

## Overview
This family encompasses techniques that generate volumetric data or manage rendering performance dynamically, rather than relying solely on static, pre-computed 3D textures. It addresses the limitations of static data in terms of memory overhead, resolution limits, and interactivity. The methods differ from standard [direct volume ray casting](#19-direct-volume-ray-casting.md) by either computing density analytically via [procedural noise functions](#1799-procedural-noise-functions.md) (e.g., [Worley noise](#1726-worley-noise.md)) during the ray march [2447-volumetric-smoke-rendering-with-worley-noise-and-light-maps.md][8240-procedural-volumetric-cloud-rendering-gpu-shader.md], applying spatial distortions to rays for focus+context [6767-gpu-accelerated-ray-casting-with-volumetric-lenses.md], modeling deformations via [inverse displacement](#10637-discontinuous-displacement-mapping-for-volume-graphics.md) mapping [10659-displacement-mapping-for-volume-rendering.md], or dynamically selecting between multi-frame rate warping and parallel raycasting based on workload complexity [11338-dynamic-multi-frame-rate-rendering.md].

## Shared principles
The family shares the fundamental [ray casting](#6080-ray-casting.md) loop structure defined in [Direct volume ray casting](19-direct-volume-ray-casting.md), but modifies the sampling stage or the rendering pipeline control flow.

1.  **Procedural Evaluation**: Instead of sampling a fixed 3D texture, density $V(\mathbf{p})$ is computed on-the-fly using mathematical functions (e.g., Fractal Brownian Motion, Worley noise) evaluated at the sample point $\mathbf{p}$ [8240-procedural-volumetric-cloud-rendering-gpu-shader.md].
2.  **Dynamic Ray Trajectories**: Rays may be distorted or redirected based on lens parameters or displacement fields, requiring custom intersection logic with the volume bounding box [6767-gpu-accelerated-ray-casting-with-volumetric-lenses.md][10659-displacement-mapping-for-volume-rendering.md].
3.  **Adaptive Rendering**: The system may switch between rendering paradigms (e.g., image warping vs. full raycasting) based on runtime metrics like resolution and sampling rate [11338-dynamic-multi-frame-rate-rendering.md].

## Subtopics

### [Volumetric Smoke Rendering with Worley Noise and Light Maps](2447-volumetric-smoke-rendering-with-worley-noise-and-light-maps.md)
Uses 3D Worley noise for density generation and light maps for scattering. Chosen for real-time animated smoke effects where memory for high-res textures is prohibitive.

### [GPU-accelerated ray casting with volumetric lenses](6767-gpu-accelerated-ray-casting-with-volumetric-lenses.md)
Applies spatially varying ray distortions for focus+context. Chosen when visualizing specific regions of interest within large datasets without occlusion.

### [Procedural Volumetric Cloud Rendering (GPU Shader)](8240-procedural-volumetric-cloud-rendering-gpu-shader.md)
Evaluates procedural noise ([FBM](#1260-3d-perlin-like-noise-and-fractal-brownian-motion-fbm.md)/Worley) directly in the fragment shader. Chosen for infinite resolution clouds and seamless animation without [pre-computation](#2330-pre-computation.md).

### [Displacement Mapping for Volume Rendering](10659-displacement-mapping-for-volume-rendering.md)
Models interactive deformations (cuts, peeling) using inverse displacement mapping. Chosen for dynamic geometric changes without mesh re-tessellation.

### [Dynamic Multi-Frame Rate Rendering](11338-dynamic-multi-frame-rate-rendering.md)
Hybrid system switching between image-based warping and parallel raycasting. Chosen to optimize the trade-off between latency and quality based on current workload complexity.

## Background
The techniques originate from the need to render complex, dynamic volumetric phenomena (smoke, clouds) and interactive deformations that cannot be efficiently stored in static voxel grids. Procedural noise methods leverage the parallelism of GPUs to compute density analytically [8240-procedural-volumetric-cloud-rendering-gpu-shader.md]. Lens techniques extend standard projection models to support interactive exploration [6767-gpu-accelerated-ray-casting-with-volumetric-lenses.md]. Displacement mapping adapts surface modeling concepts to volume data for interactive editing [10659-displacement-mapping-for-volume-rendering.md]. Multi-frame rate rendering addresses the performance bottlenecks of high-resolution raycasting in distributed or multi-GPU environments [11338-dynamic-multi-frame-rate-rendering.md].
